ticket.title: In module configuration pages, the "Activate module for this shop context" checkbox does not work
ticket.bug:
When the multistore option is activated and at least two shops have been created, a new panel is displayed at the bottom of module configuration pages, containing a checkbox labeled "Activate module for this shop context". Checking/unchecking this checkbox is supposed to enable/disable the current module for the current shop context.

This does not currently work. Accessing a module's configuration page from a context where it is disabled and clicking  the checkbox to activate it just reloads the page, leaving the module deactivated and reseting the checkbox to its unchecked state.
ticket.expected: Checking the box should systematically enable the module for the current context, and unchecking it should disable it.
ticket.steps:
1. Activate the multistore feature if disabled, in Parameters > General > Enable Multistore
2. Access Multistore in Advanced Parameters and create one if only one exists
3. Install a module that has a configuration page, like the Contact form module for example
4. Access its configuration page from the context of a shop where it's enabled, and then swap to the new shop
5. It will show as disabled by default. Check the "Activate module for this shop context" box.
6. The page reloads showing the checkbox unchecked, and the module is still disabled in this context

resolution.title: Fix module activation checkbox in module configuration pages
resolution.description: When the multishop option is activated and at least two shops have been created, a new panel is displayed at the bottom of module configuration pages, containing a checkbox labeled "Activate module for this shop context". Checking/unchecking this checkbox is supposed to enable/disable the current module for the current shop context.  This does not currently work. Clicking this box reloads the current url, adding an "enable" parameter with a value of 0 or 1 depending on if it is checked or not. Getting the status of the checkbox is achieved via the jquery .attr() method, which since jQuery 1.6 cannot be used for attributes like "checked" or "disabled". As a result "enable" is set to 0 wether the box is checked or not.  The solution is to use jQuery's .is(':checked') method instead.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Activate the multistore feature if disabled, in Parameters > General > Enable Multistore  2. Access Multistore in Advanced Parameters and create one if only one exists  3. Install a module that has a configuration page, like the Contact form module for example  4. Access its configuration page from the context of a shop where it's enabled, and then swap to the new shop  5. It will show as disabled by default. Check the "Activate module for this shop context" box.  6. The page reloads showing the checkbox checked, and the module enabled in this context
resolution.author: IcarusSosie

ticket.title: Smarty template caching Module::isCached() faulty causes performance loss
ticket.bug:
Prestashop class **Module** (`Prestashop /classes/module/Module.php`) has a function called **isCached** to check if tpl file is cached. This function fails to check and returns **false** while tpl is cached. 

Commit https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/13804

Person who made PR was fixing issue #9763 and modified Module's class function **fetch** adding this:

```
if ($compile_id === null) {
            $compile_id = Context::getContext()->shop->theme->getName();
        }
```
Because of this change when you call **fetch** function with **$compile_id = null** it generates smarty cache file under $compile_id directory which is theme name in this case (if $compile_id is null then $compile_id is set to theme name).

But when you try to check if template is cached with function **isCached** with **$compile_id = null** you always get **false** because code added in **fetch** function should be also added to **isCached** function.

Templates are fetched (cached) under compile_id which is theme name in most cases, but isCached function checks if template is cached with empty compile_id which causes false result.

**This bug causes a huge performance issues.** Many plugins check if tpl is cached and if not - they perform data aggregation and assignation for smarty to render tpl but actually is not needed.

resolution.title: Fix performance issue on Smarty template caching
resolution.description: From 1.7.7.0 version Module class function isCached fails to check if tpl is cached. This PR fixes that.
resolution.how_to_test: In order to test if it is fixed you need to check if function isCached works properly or try to reproduce issue. How to reproduce issue is described in issue ticket.
resolution.author: lukaslau

resolution.title: Fix module activation checkbox in module configuration pages
resolution.description: When the multishop option is activated and at least two shops have been created, a new panel is displayed at the bottom of module configuration pages, containing a checkbox labeled "Activate module for this shop context". Checking/unchecking this checkbox is supposed to enable/disable the current module for the current shop context.  This does not currently work. Clicking this box reloads the current url, adding an "enable" parameter with a value of 0 or 1 depending on if it is checked or not. Getting the status of the checkbox is achieved via the jquery .attr() method, which since jQuery 1.6 cannot be used for attributes like "checked" or "disabled". As a result "enable" is set to 0 wether the box is checked or not.  The solution is to use jQuery's .is(':checked') method instead.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Activate the multistore feature if disabled, in Parameters > General > Enable Multistore  2. Access Multistore in Advanced Parameters and create one if only one exists  3. Install a module that has a configuration page, like the Contact form module for example  4. Access its configuration page from the context of a shop where it's enabled, and then swap to the new shop  5. It will show as disabled by default. Check the "Activate module for this shop context" box.  6. The page reloads showing the checkbox checked, and the module enabled in this context

ticket.title: Smarty template caching Module::isCached() faulty causes performance loss
ticket.bug:
Prestashop class **Module** (`Prestashop /classes/module/Module.php`) has a function called **isCached** to check if tpl file is cached. This function fails to check and returns **false** while tpl is cached. 

Commit https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/13804

Person who made PR was fixing issue #9763 and modified Module's class function **fetch** adding this:

```
if ($compile_id === null) {
            $compile_id = Context::getContext()->shop->theme->getName();
        }
```
Because of this change when you call **fetch** function with **$compile_id = null** it generates smarty cache file under $compile_id directory which is theme name in this case (if $compile_id is null then $compile_id is set to theme name).

But when you try to check if template is cached with function **isCached** with **$compile_id = null** you always get **false** because code added in **fetch** function should be also added to **isCached** function.

Templates are fetched (cached) under compile_id which is theme name in most cases, but isCached function checks if template is cached with empty compile_id which causes false result.

**This bug causes a huge performance issues.** Many plugins check if tpl is cached and if not - they perform data aggregation and assignation for smarty to render tpl but actually is not needed.

resolution.title: Fix performance issue on Smarty template caching
resolution.description: From 1.7.7.0 version Module class function isCached fails to check if tpl is cached. This PR fixes that.
resolution.how_to_test: In order to test if it is fixed you need to check if function isCached works properly or try to reproduce issue. How to reproduce issue is described in issue ticket.
resolution.author: lukaslau
